rule: Declare one key light per film in the film.html header: direction, colour hex, softness, intensity
why: A stated light is the thing every shading decision traces back to; with no declared key there is no lit side and no shade side
numbers: 1 key light per film; direction in {top-left,top,side,back}; softness in {hard,soft,very soft}; intensity 0-100%
do: Write KEY/FILL/RIM/AMBIENT into the header block: KEY top-left #FFD9B0 soft 100, FILL 22%, RIM on 3px, AMBIENT 12%
antipattern: Objects sitting in an evenly lit field with no source anywhere in frame

rule: Every object shows a lit side and a shade side, driven by the declared key
why: Real materials are read by the ratio between lit and unlit value; when that ratio is constant the brain reads coloured shape instead of material
numbers: lit:shade value ratio >= 1.35:1 in L*; shade side >= 20% darker than base
do: Pick the side away from the key and darken it by >= 20%; the terminator must be soft, never a hard polyline
antipattern: A perfectly vertical even gradient from lid to base with no falloff, no core shadow, no bounce

rule: Build the shading stack in this order: base gradient, core shadow, contact shadow, rim highlight, ambient falloff
why: Each term answers a different perceptual question; skipping one makes the object read as a sticker
numbers: 5 terms; core shadow >= 20% darker; rim 2-4px at 1080 width; ambient corners >= 10% L* darker than centre
do: For each object: linear or radial base, shade side, tight dark ellipse under it, one bright edge toward key, corner vignette
antipattern: One flat fill used for every material in the film

rule: Put a contact/occlusion shadow under everything grounded
why: It is the cheapest single fix for objects that float; without it a prop sits on the frame rather than in the world
numbers: short dark ellipse, alpha 30-50%, tight to the base (width ~1.15x base width, height 8-14% of it)
do: ctx.ellipse at the base point, black at 0.35 alpha with a radial gradient to transparent, drawn before the object
antipattern: Objects hovering with no ground contact shading (s09 jars, s10 billets)

rule: Give every non-flat object one rim or edge highlight toward the key
why: A single rim is what makes flat vector colour read as lit illustration
numbers: 1 rim per object; width 2-4px at 1080 width; lightness above base by >= 15% L*
do: Stroke the key-facing contour with a light-tinted line or draw a thin bright arc along it
antipattern: Flat two-tone shapes with no edge response at all

rule: Darken the frame corners by at least 10% L* relative to the centre
why: Without corner falloff the frame reads as a wall poster, not a lens
numbers: corners >= 10% L* darker than centre in every frame; vignette alpha 0.45-0.65 at the extreme corner
do: One radial gradient drawn last (or in the grade pass) from transparent at 55% radius to shadow-2 at 62% alpha at the corner
antipattern: Evenly lit full-frame field

rule: Keep a cool fill under about 25% of the total light and state it as fill
why: Mixing a warm key with an unstated cool shadow looks like two lighting setups fighting
numbers: cool fill <= 25% of light contribution; if exceeded, restate the light model
do: multiply the whole frame with rgba(coolfill,0.20) once in the grade to hold shadows above black
antipattern: Warm key and cold shadow with no declared relationship

rule: Build atmosphere light from elongated soft radial pools with falloff, never from a clipped polygon
why: Any clip region filled by a gradient that is non-zero at the clip edge produces a hard straight edge and the eye reads a decal, not light
numbers: core peak alpha ~0.14; anything above ~0.25 stops being light; 2 nested pools (tight core + wide penumbra); outermost stop fully transparent
do: translate(x,cy) then scale(rx/ry,1) then a radial gradient to transparent, on globalCompositeOperation lighter, no clip path
antipattern: A striped orange polygon with hard edges reading as hazard tape printed on the deck

rule: House the key in the frame: a viewer must be able to point at the light source and trace its effect on two surfaces
why: An unexplained highlight band is a smudge; a sourced one is cinematography
numbers: 1 hero lit frame per film; the source visible in frame; its effect readable on >= 2 surfaces
do: Put the practical (lamp, port, sign) in shot and show its pool on the wall and its rim on the prop
antipattern: A highlight band with nothing in the scene explaining where it comes from

rule: Reject semi-transparent grey ellipses standing in for light
why: Grey ellipses with no source and no falloff read as smudges on the lens
numbers: falloff must reach full transparency at the edge; use the palette key hue, not grey
do: Replace the grey ellipse with a radial pool in the key hue on lighter blend
antipattern: s12 searchlight ellipses: grey, no source, no falloff

rule: Scale every emissive treatment as a function of its host object size
why: A fixed-radius glow is correct on a hero and absurd on a quarter-size still-life part; three of them blow the accent budget in one frame
do: Multiply glow radius and alpha by the host's height ratio inside the object's own draw call
antipattern: Three identical orange rings on three mini billets at once

rule: Cap emissive/signal light at one instance per frame
why: Emissive light is the film's attention currency; two competing ones cancel each other
numbers: max 1 emissive accent per frame; max 2 signal uses per scene
do: Draw the emissive port only where the frame wants the eye; suppress the others
antipattern: Three orange emissive ports in one macro frame

rule: Separate adjacent depth planes by at least 15% L*
why: If two planes share a value they fuse into one flat field and the depth model collapses
numbers: >= 15% L* between adjacent planes; >= 15% L* between subject and environment inside a plane
do: Compute the plane base values from the palette page/surface/shadow tokens, then widen the gap until >= 15% L*
antipattern: Foreground, subject and background all sitting in the same value band

rule: Draw atmosphere both behind and in front of the subject
why: Atmosphere only behind reads as a background texture; a few particles in front sell a volume
numbers: foreground motes 6-14 visible sprites per frame, alpha 0.06-0.20, sizes 2-9px, one plane blurred
do: Depth-sort motes by a noise(t) depth key and draw the nearest ones after the subject
antipattern: Dust drawn only as a static background texture

rule: State one light temperature per film and derive every gradient, glow and shadow tint from it
why: A film whose warms and cools come from different worlds never coheres into one film
numbers: 1 temperature token per film; every gradient stop is a tint of it; cool fill <= 25%
do: Put the key hue in the header and compute all ramp stop colours as HSL shifts of it
antipattern: Warm amber field cut against a cold blue end card world

rule: Declare the shadow ladder as three steps of the page hue, never black and never grey
why: Black shadows are the fastest way to make a vector film look like a template
numbers: shadow-1/2/3 = page hue at 3 darker steps; L* drop per step 8-14
do: Compute shadow tokens from --page in HSL, keep saturation, subtract lightness
antipattern: Flat black drop shadows reused on every card

rule: Give glass a specular streak, an edge and a thickness term, or do not draw glass
why: There is no refraction term in canvas2d, so a 1px outlined ellipse degrades to a wireframe and reads unfinished
numbers: >= 3 terms: 1 specular streak 2-5px, 1 bright edge arc, 1 darker inner band; stroke width >= 2px at 1080
do: Draw a translucent radial body, a bright angled streak, and a rim arc; never a bare stroke ellipse
antipattern: Three 1px outlined ellipses with no highlight, thickness or rim

rule: Practice the reference lighting model already proven in the batch (s08 pendant lamp pool with dust and bokeh)
why: It is the one good lighting idea the studio already produced; reuse the mechanism rather than inventing a new one
numbers: pool >= 1.2x the hero's width; dust 20-40 motes; bokeh <= 30 sprites at alpha 0.06-0.18
do: Copy the s08 scene structure: practical lamp, soft pool on the wall, motes in the beam, defocused bokeh behind
antipattern: A flat wall with no practical and no pool

rule: Build at least three distinct planes in every scene: foreground, subject, environment
why: A scene with one plane is a sticker sheet; three planes with different value and detail read as space for free
numbers: 3 planes minimum; value gap >= 15% L* between adjacent planes; environment carries the lowest detail
do: Draw background first, then subject, then a foreground occluder crossing a frame edge
antipattern: One flat stage reused for every scene of the film

rule: Put an occluding foreground element at a frame edge in at least one scene per film in both ratios
why: A foreground occluder is the cheapest depth cue there is and it costs one shape
numbers: 1 occluder per scene minimum; it must cross the frame edge; blur or darken it by 10-25%
do: A beam, a rail, a shoulder of furniture, a blurred shape crossing bottom or side
antipattern: Everything sitting at the same depth, nothing near the lens

rule: Blur and darken the background plane relative to the subject
why: Out-of-focus background is a focus differential, which reads as a lens; equal sharpness everywhere reads as a diagram
numbers: background ctx.filter blur 3-8px at 1080 width; background detail count < 40% of the subject's
do: Set ctx.filter = blur on the background pass, reset it before the subject
antipattern: Background as sharp and as detailed as the subject

rule: Give the background more grain/atmosphere than the subject
why: Grain is a depth cue as much as a texture: more atmosphere reads as further away
numbers: background grain alpha 6-10% vs foreground 2-4%
do: Draw the grain overlay clipped to the background band, or draw a second weaker pass over the subject
antipattern: One uniform grain layer over everything at one strength

rule: Replace decorative wallpaper grids with a room that has a material and a horizon
why: A decoration identical in every shot stops being space and becomes a watermark
numbers: 1 horizon or floor line per scene; wall plane value range spans >= 12% L* across the frame
do: Give the wall a gradient along the key axis, put the floor on its own value, and meet them on the shared line
antipattern: A navy/green/brown/purple flat field with the same overlaid graph grid in all of them

rule: Make wall and floor planes share their boundary line exactly
why: A gap between drawn planes leaves stale pixels from the previously sought frame, which is a correctness bug under out-of-order seek and a visible seam otherwise
numbers: wall bottom y must equal floor top y exactly, both ratios
do: Compute one horizon constant per ratio from the layout table and use it in both painters
antipattern: Floor drawn from y=700 and wall drawn to y=640 on a frame sought out of order

rule: Use 3-6 parallax planes with graduated motion ratios instead of one moving layer
why: Multiplane parallax is the oldest and still the cheapest way to make flat art feel dimensional
numbers: 3-6 layers; motion ratio between adjacent layers 0.15-0.35; nearest layer up to 1.25x base drift
do: Drive each layer's x from the same camera parameter times its own ratio
antipattern: All layers translating by the same amount

rule: Treat deliberately empty regions as designed forms, not leftovers
why: Negative space that is the remainder of a layout reads as an unfinished frame; a wedge or a pool reads as intent
numbers: every empty region must be a named form; a frame > 60% undifferentiated empty field is a defect
do: Name the negative shape in the scene table (a diagonal, a wedge, a light pool) and draw it
antipattern: Bottom 40-45% of every frame a dead striped floor

rule: Never ship a scene that is more than 60% blank field
why: Two scenes at 90-95% blank paper read as running out of things to draw
numbers: blank-field share <= 60% of frame area in every scene; measure it on the still
do: Open the scene with content already present; add a foreground plane rather than shrinking the layout
antipattern: ~90% and ~95% blank cream scenes back to back

rule: Vary the background family between consecutive scenes
why: The audience learns a repeated template by scene two and stops watching
numbers: no two consecutive scenes share background family; >= 3 distinct background families per film
do: Write the background family of every scene into the scene table and diff consecutive rows
antipattern: s10: seven frames, one identical stage

rule: Add a haze or fog term between the environment and the camera
why: Aerial perspective separates planes additively instead of by drawing more shapes
numbers: haze alpha 8-18% of the environment colour, densest at the horizon
do: One flat rectangle in the page hue at low alpha between the background and the subject
antipattern: Background meeting the subject at a hard value change with nothing between

rule: Scale the depth rig with the framing in macro scenes
why: A rig left at world scale next to a magnified part reads as a toy standing in a wall
numbers: wrap in translate(anchor) scale(k) translate(-anchor); k = 1.55 for an extreme-macro tool in the s10 case
do: Apply the scale inside the prop's own branch so its anchor stays where the framing wants it
antipattern: A drill rig visibly the wrong size against a magnified part

rule: Ban the flat single fill: every material is built from at least two of {gradient, rim, occlusion, grain, blend mode}
why: Every real material has a tell; one flat fill for all of them flattens the film onto a single plane
numbers: >= 2 of 5 treatments per material; materials kit of 5-6 named treatments per film
do: Define matte/paper/metal/glass/emissive once and reuse them; each is a function, not a colour
antipattern: A pure white polygon with a hard edge reading as a torn scrap

rule: Define a materials kit of 5-6 named treatments and reuse it deliberately
why: Reuse is what makes a film look art-directed instead of improvised per prop
numbers: matte, paper, metal, glass, emissive, glass-over-X; each with >= 2 terms and a scale function
do: Write the kit as PA helpers: material.metal(ctx, path, h), material.paper(...), each taking object height
antipattern: Each prop inventing its own shading from scratch

rule: Give paper fibre, a soft fold and a slightly uneven edge
why: Paper with a perfectly straight edge and no fibre reads as a torn scrap or a rectangle
numbers: fibre grain 3-6% alpha at 2-4px scale; fold = a linear value shift of 6-12% L* across the sheet
do: One feTurbulence-derived tile at low alpha plus one wide linear gradient across the sheet
antipattern: A pure white polygon with a hard edge

rule: Metal needs a two-tone reflection plus an environment line plus an edge highlight
why: Metal is read from the horizon line inside the object; without it, a grey shape is just grey
numbers: >= 3 terms; dark band 35-55% of the object height; bright band 45-65%; edge highlight 1-3px
do: Split the billet/cylinder into a dark lower band and a bright upper band with a hard-ish horizon and a bright contour on the key side
antipattern: One small baked gradient reused at 1/4 size on three props

rule: Emissive materials get a two-stop glow with true falloff plus a hot core
why: A flat orange port is a shape; a port with a hot core and a wide falloff is light
numbers: core alpha 0.85-1.0 at <= 0.35x radius; falloff to 0 at 1.6-2.2x radius; <= 1 per frame
do: Draw the body, then a radial gradient in lighter blend, then a 2-3px near-white core
antipattern: A flat orange rectangle with no glow at all

rule: Give a frosted glass panel a rim and an inner shadow, not a flat rounded rect
why: UI panels are a designed material; a flat rounded rect is the tell of a placeholder
numbers: frost alpha 0.10-0.22; inner shadow 8-14% L* darker at the top edge; rim 1-2px at 60-80% alpha
do: blur a copy of the background through the panel rect, then draw the rim and an inner top shadow
antipattern: Identical flat rounded rects with the same soft drop shadow stacked at random angles

rule: Fill every material gradient along the declared light axis, not along the object's own symmetry
why: A gradient that ignores the light is the reason props look pasted on the wall
numbers: gradient angle within 20 degrees of the key direction for every lit object
do: Compute gradient endpoints from the key direction vector, once per film
antipattern: A vertical gradient on an object lit from the side

rule: Kill copy-pasted duplicate props: vary rotation, occlusion and depth or use a single hero
why: Three copies of the hero asset at 1/4 scale read as a copy-paste, not as a row of objects
numbers: if N > 1: rotation varies >= 3 degrees, depth varies >= 12% scale, and each is separately occluded
do: Draw each instance from its own seeded parameters (rotation, y, scale, occlusion order)
antipattern: Three identical mini billets on a wooden base with one soft shadow

rule: Cut props that can never beat a photograph out of the film, or stylise them fully
why: The medium has no raster, no illustration and no refraction, so anything that must look like a real object is capped
numbers: glass/refraction register: unreachable; stylised flat-material register: reachable in canvas2d
do: Choose scenes that live in the reachable register instead of promising product photography
antipattern: A hero jar asked to look like a product photo in a vector film

rule: Never let an object be a bare stroke outline with no fill and no thickness
why: A bare outline is read as an unfinished drawing, which is exactly the audit verdict on the s08 bowl
numbers: stroke width >= 2px at 1080; every closed shape has a fill or an explicit open-form intent
do: Fill first, then stroke; if the object is genuinely line art, vary stroke weight with zoom (pa-ink strokePx)
antipattern: A 1px outlined ellipse set standing for a glass bowl

rule: Use eight named type roles: display, headline, deck, body, label, legal, numeral, button
why: A hierarchy is a relationship, not a size ladder; without named roles every line is the same line at different sizes
numbers: 8 roles; display 96-132px weight 800-900; headline 56-72px 600-700; deck 34-40px 300-400; body 28-32px 400; label 20-24px 500-600; legal 16-18px 300; numeral weight 700-800 at 1.4x its element; button 30-34px 600
do: Define one PA.type object per ratio with role, size, weight, lineHeight, colour and tracking
antipattern: A single Vazirmatn face at 2-3 sizes carrying every word in the film

rule: Force two-axis contrast: at least one adjacent role pair differs by >= 200 weight units AND >= 1.5x size
why: Size alone reads as one line that got smaller; weight plus proportion reads as two designed roles
numbers: weight delta >= 200 axis units; size ratio >= 1.5 between adjacent roles
do: Pair label 600/22px with headline 800/66px, plus a rule device
antipattern: Headline and sub-line the same white and the same weight, differing only in point size

rule: Use a weight gap of >= 300 axis units inside one family; 300/400/500 is forbidden
why: Two adjacent weight steps read as a mistake rather than as hierarchy
numbers: 250 / 550 / 850 is a clean three-step system; contrast >= 300 axis units
do: Pick two or three instances from the variable axis far apart, never neighbouring
antipattern: A 400 deck against a 500 label

rule: Cap at three type roles per frame, and count the numeral as one of the three
why: Four live text blocks in one frame is a layout failure, not richness
numbers: <= 3 roles per frame including numeral; one live text block per region always
do: In a MEASURE frame show label + numeral, or headline + numeral, never all four
antipattern: label + headline + deck + numeral all live in one MEASURE frame

rule: Express every type size in px against a 1080 short-axis reference, so both ratios get identical optical size
why: Both canvases are 1080 on the short axis, so a min(W,H) reference produces the same optical size in 9:16 and 16:9; only measure and column count change
do: Compute sizes once from min(W,H) and reuse the same numbers in both ratio branches
antipattern: Bigger type in the landscape cut because the canvas is wider

rule: Keep the 1080-reference modular ladder; never jump 3+ steps inside one frame's visual group
why: The ladder keeps optical relationships stable across shots; a 3-step jump destroys the relationship the ladder encodes
do: Read the size from the ladder table rather than choosing a number per scene
antipattern: A 260px display beside a 24px label with nothing between

rule: Hold the landscape measure to two columns of ~700px, never one 1500px line
why: At 40px a 1500px measure is about 90 Persian characters per line, which is unreadable
numbers: 9:16 body measure 700px (~45-55 Persian chars); 16:9 two columns of 700px with a 120px gutter; display measure 940px tall / 1400px wide max
do: Put the column count in the per-ratio layout table and wrap at the column edge
antipattern: A single wide measure in 16:9 running the full frame width

rule: Meet the contrast floors against the actual pixels behind the text
why: Nominal background contrast is a fiction when a gradient or scenery sits behind the type
numbers: body >= 4.5:1; large text >= 3:1; measured on the rendered still, not on the token values
do: Sample the frame behind each text block and compute the ratio; fix by scrim, knockout or value shift
antipattern: White display type over blue domes with 8px grey labels behind it

rule: Text over scenery requires a knockout, a scrim at 55-75%, or >= 45% L* value separation
why: Readable-enough is not a standard; one of three mechanical conditions must hold
numbers: scrim = shadow-2 field at 55-75% alpha; or value separation >= 45% L*; or the shape behind is punched
do: Draw the scrim before the text and keep it inside the text envelope plus 24px
antipattern: A headline crossing the jar lid with nothing behind it

rule: Give the label role a graphic device: a short accent rule above the label, right-aligned to its measured width
why: Weight 600 at 22px against a 700/66px headline is not enough contrast on its own; the rule is a second axis that size cannot fake
numbers: rule height 3-4px; width = measured label width; gap 10-14px; colour is signal or accent, never the body colour
do: ctx.measureText(label).width then fillRect above it, inset by one pixel so it reads as a rule and not a bar
antipattern: Label carried by colour alone with no device

rule: One display line per film carrying the claim
why: If two lines claim the display role, neither lands as the film's statement
numbers: 1 display block per film; 1-3 words; 96-132px at 1080 reference
do: Reserve the display role in the header for the single claim and give every other line a smaller role
antipattern: Every scene title set at display scale

rule: Set the numeral role from a Persian-digit family that is the same family as the surrounding text, or a deliberate display face used throughout
why: Latin display numerals dropped into a Persian layout have no design relationship to the text around them
numbers: numeral role weight 700-800; figure 120px, unit 28px; U+06F0-06F9 only
do: Wrap numerals in one span with the numeral family and use it in every stat frame of the film
antipattern: A Latin-display counter with a different family and optical weight from the Persian copy

rule: Never put Latin display numerals inside a Persian layout
why: The counter's face is part of the type system; a foreign numeral face breaks it
numbers: 0 Latin numeral runs; digits only from U+06F0-06F9
do: Check every numeral run for the Persian block and grep the film for 0-9 inside Persian strings
antipattern: A Latin-display numeral dropped into a Persian HUD

rule: Bump Persian size 5-10% or one weight step above the Latin spec it came from
why: Persian at a nominal weight reads lighter than Latin at the same weight; a Latin 800 hero wants a Persian 900
numbers: +5-10% size or +1 weight step; a Latin-800 hero maps to Persian 900 or a display face
do: Apply the bump once in the type table, not per scene
antipattern: Latin and Persian copy matched at the same weight and size

rule: Never fake bold on a single-weight face: asking for 600/800 from a one-weight font smears the letterforms
why: Only Vazirmatn, Estedad, Noto Kufi Arabic and Sahel give the 100-900 range; the other faces in our pool have one weight
numbers: single-weight faces: Lalezar, Aref Ruqaa, Amiri, Katibeh, Gulzar, Gandom, Shabnam, Samim, Parastoo, Nahid, Tanha, Scheherazade New, Lateef, Vazirmatn-RD
do: Emphasise with size or colour, or fake weight with a matching WebkitTextStroke where fill and stroke match
antipattern: Requesting weight 700 from Lalezar and shipping a smeared headline

rule: Never build hollow/outline Persian type with -webkit-text-stroke
why: alreq-gap #220 shows the stroke interrupting the cursive flow at every join in Gecko, Blink and WebKit, and CSS has no text-stroke
numbers: 0 uses of -webkit-text-stroke as an outline on joined Persian; alternative: 2x stroke plus paint-order stroke fill with an opaque fill, or SVG feMorphology dilate-erode
do: If an outline is wanted, draw two offset copies or dilate the path; keep the fill opaque so joins stay visible
antipattern: A stroked outline Persian headline with gaps at every join

rule: Set line-height >= 1.4 for Naskh display, >= 1.6 for body, >= 1.9-2.2 for Nastaliq
why: Persian ascenders and descenders are longer than Latin, so Latin line-height clips the dots above and the yeh below
numbers: 1.4 display Naskh; 1.6 body; 1.9-2.2 Nastaliq; a Persian mask container needs the full line box >= 1.5em
do: Put lineHeight in the type role table, never a Latin default
antipattern: Dots of پ چ ژ and the descender of ی clipped at line-height 1

rule: Push underlines and overlines further from the baseline than the Latin offset
why: Persian ascenders and descenders are longer and the rule must not cross the descender ink (alreq-gap #223)
numbers: offset >= 1.35x the Latin offset; clearance >= 6px at 1080 from the measured descender bottom
do: Measure the ink box of the actual string and place the rule below it
antipattern: A Latin-tuned underline floating 40px low (recorded in brand-ink-open)

rule: Derive type offsets from the measured ink box of the real string, not from Latin cap/x-height numbers
why: Persian has no cap-height discipline; aligning to a Latin line-box centre puts the title visibly high or low
numbers: measure ink box via measureText actualBoundingBoxAscent/Descent; never hard-code a Latin character-width grid
do: Measure the ink box per string at the real size and align on its centre or its own baseline
antipattern: Aligning a Persian title to the line-box centre and getting a visibly low title

rule: Ban text-transform and any fake italic/skew on Persian
why: Persian has no case and no italic; uppercase is meaningless and a skew is a fake
numbers: 0 uses of text-transform on Persian runs; 0 skewX used as emphasis
do: Recover hierarchy with size, weight, colour and the label rule device
antipattern: A skewed Persian headline used as emphasis

rule: Reserve the layout box with a hidden ghost copy at the final weight whenever animating weight
why: Weight animation re-shapes and re-lays out the run every frame, so the line can reflow and push neighbours mid-shot
numbers: ghost copy at final weight reserves width; animated run in a fixed-size box; <= 1 animated text node per shot
do: Draw the ghost string first at weight 850 in the box, then draw the animated run on top
antipattern: A weight-pumped headline shifting its neighbours every frame

rule: Animate weight only; we hold no Persian face with a width or optical-size axis
why: Every variable Persian face in the pool has a wght axis only, so width ideas must use kashida or scaleX instead
numbers: wght 100..900 (Vazirmatn, Estedad, NotoKufiArabic); 400..900 (Sahel); 300..700 (Lemonada); no wdth, no opsz anywhere in the pool
do: Use font-variation-settings wght for a weight pump; use kashida or <= 4% scaleX for width
antipattern: Animating a wdth axis that does not exist and silently getting nothing

rule: Keep scaleX stretch under about 4% and never use it as the primary width device
why: scaleX scales the already-rasterised glyph, thinning verticals and thickening horizontals unevenly
numbers: scaleX <= 1.04; prefer kashida; a real wdth axis would be correct but we do not hold one
do: If a stretch is unavoidable, hold it under 4% and pair it with a size increase
antipattern: A naive scaleX stretch used as a spacing substitute

rule: Set a maximum of two live-text blocks per region and separate them by >= 1.5x the larger cap height or an explicit rule
why: Two blocks in one region is the mechanism behind the batch's worst frame, where a headline was printed across a certificate's own text
numbers: 2 blocks max per region; gap >= 1.5x cap height of the larger block, or an explicit rule/divider
do: Define regions per ratio in the layout table and assert no two blocks' boxes intersect
antipattern: The white headline printed straight across the certificate text

rule: Never let any text be clipped by the canvas edge or leave the text envelope
why: Clipped type is the exact failure a viewer reads as nobody looked at this
numbers: 9:16 envelope 72px sides, 140px top, 180px bottom; 16:9 envelope 96px sides, 64px top and bottom; nothing outside it
do: Check the envelope on the final frames of both ratios and on every still
antipattern: A bottom headline clipped by the canvas edge

rule: Put every text block on one 8px baseline grid shared by all scenes
why: A shared baseline grid is what makes consecutive frames read as one film
numbers: 8px baseline grid; all text block y positions are multiples of 8
do: Round every text y in the layout table to a multiple of 8 and reuse the table across scenes
antipattern: A caption block that drifts between two scenes instead of holding its baseline

rule: Keep exactly one white token in the film and use it everywhere white is needed
why: Two slightly different whites always read as an accident
numbers: 1 white token; 0 pairs of near-white fills within 3% L* of each other
do: Declare --white once and check that no card uses a second off-white fill
antipattern: An off-white page and a pure-white card fill in the same film

rule: Probe Persian glyph coverage of any candidate face before it ships
why: A face that lacks Persian ی/ک or ZWNJ handling silently falls back and the film looks unstyled
numbers: probe string covers ی ک پ چ ژ گ آ ه ئ ء ZWNJ and U+06F0-06F9
do: Render the probe string in the harness and look at it before adding the face to the film
antipattern: A face whose Persian falls back to a system font with no one noticing

rule: Apply letter-spacing: 0 to every Persian run, always
why: Letter-spacing is applied after shaping as an advance between glyph positions, so the ink stops touching and the cursive join is visually severed
numbers: 0 letter-spacing on Persian; tracking is a Latin-only device (label and legal roles in Latin, or never)
do: Set letterSpacing 0 on every canvas text call and never put tracking in a Persian type role
antipattern: A tracked-out Persian headline whose letters came apart

rule: Treat letter-spacing breaking Persian as an open engine bug, not a font choice
why: Chromium issue 40618336 is titled letter spacing should not break Arabic words and is open; implementations guess by script
numbers: issue 40618336 open; CSSWG question on Arabic digits open
do: Do not try to solve it by choosing another face; remove the tracking
antipattern: Assuming a different font will fix a tracked Persian line

rule: Never split Persian text per code point: each element becomes its own shaping context and renders in isolated form
why: A joining segment is shaped per run; splitting the run destroys the initial/medial/final forms
numbers: 4 positional forms per letter; splitting a word yields isolated forms such as ز و د instead of زودتر
do: Split at word level, or at closed joining segment level at most
antipattern: Per-letter spans producing ز و د تر ا ر سا ل کن

rule: Never give a per-character or per-word Persian span a non-zero margin, padding or border
why: alreq-gap #222 resolved: non-zero margin/padding/border and isolation boundaries break the join
numbers: margin 0, padding 0, border 0 on any inline span inside a Persian word
do: Use the parent's letter positions or a transform on the whole run; do not pad the span
antipattern: Padded per-character spans splitting a Persian word into disconnected letters

rule: Avoid inline-block cells for Persian units; an atomic inline is an isolation boundary and breaks joins
why: The boundary-shaping rules forbid atomic inlines inside a joining run
numbers: display inline-block forbidden inside a Persian word; use inline with nowrap for unbreakability
do: For a split-flap or odometer, use one cell per whole word or per closed joining segment
antipattern: A per-letter cell board showing isolated forms

rule: Rank Persian split units: whole word, then closed joining segment, then growing prefix, then line mask
why: Each unit down the list carries more shaping risk; the first is correct by construction and the last re-shapes nothing
numbers: whole word = 1 shaping run; segment = started in non-join-to-right and ended in non-join-to-left form; line mask = 0 re-shaping
do: Choose the highest safe unit for the effect and state it in the recipe
antipattern: Reaching for a character split because the effect is easier to write

rule: Add U+200C between the visible prefix and the hidden remainder of a typeOn reveal
why: Without it the last visible letter takes the wrong positional form as the prefix grows
numbers: 1 ZWNJ at the prefix boundary every frame of a typeOn
do: canvas: fillText(shown + U+200C + rest) with the remainder clipped, or draw only the prefix with the ZWNJ appended
antipattern: A typeOn where each newly revealed letter snaps to a medial form

rule: Never split a base letter from its diacritic, and never transform an individual glyph that carries marks
why: Marks are positioned by GPOS mark/mkmk at shaping time, so the cluster must be shaped as one run
numbers: harakat range U+064B-U+0652; the cluster is one shaping unit
do: Transform the ancestor (translate/scale/rotate/blur) so the composed glyph layer moves whole
antipattern: A per-glyph animation that leaves the diacritics behind

rule: Transform the ancestor element, never the individual glyph, when scaling Persian
why: A transform on an ancestor transforms the already composed glyph layer, so marks stay attached and correctly offset
numbers: scale/rotate/translate/skew/opacity/blur all safe on an ancestor; per-glyph transform is not
do: Wrap the run in a group and apply ctx.translate/scale before drawing the whole run
antipattern: Scaling single glyphs and watching the dots drift

rule: Keep every ZWNJ word unbreakable with a nowrap inline span, never inline-block
why: Browsers treat ZWNJ as a line-break opportunity, so a naive wrap splits میشود into می and شود
numbers: nowrap span per ZWNJ word; 0 inline-block use for this; 0 orphans at a line end
do: Wrap each ZWNJ word in span white-space nowrap (verified by render before relying on it)
antipattern: A line ending in a single orphan letter after a ZWNJ break

rule: Never use word-break break-all, overflow-wrap anywhere, or hyphenation on Persian
why: Both can break mid-join and Persian has no hyphenation practice here
numbers: 0 uses of break-all / anywhere / hyphens on Persian
do: Widen the measure, reduce the size one ladder step, or break the line manually
antipattern: A Persian word split mid-join because the box was narrow

rule: Break Persian lines manually from an explicit line array, never by a live browser wrap
why: Browser wrapping inside an animating element reflows and can change the line count between frames, which breaks seek purity
numbers: explicit line arrays; 0 live wraps in a film; line count constant for all t
do: Write the lines in the scene table and draw them from the array
antipattern: A headline whose line count changes mid-shot as the weight animates

rule: Use only Persian digits U+06F0-06F9 and only Persian ی/ک
why: Persian digits are not the Arabic-Indic set, not Urdu shapes and not Latin; Arabic yeh/kaf in a Persian headline is immediately visible
numbers: U+06F0-06F9 only; ی U+06CC and ک U+06A9 only
do: Grep the film source for U+0660-0669, U+064A and U+0643 before capture
antipattern: An Arabic-form digit or Arabic yeh shipping in a Persian film

rule: Set Persian digits from a Persian-digit face even when the line uses another family
why: Lemonada's ۴ is the Arabic form and Nastaliq faces carry Urdu digit shapes, so digits must be served by a family that is known good
numbers: numeral span family = Vazirmatn or Estedad; or a unicode-range restricted @font-face for U+06F0-06F9
do: Give the numeral span its own family token in the type table
antipattern: Numbers set in a display face whose ۴ is the Arabic form

rule: Isolate only the numeral run with LRI U+2066 and PDI U+2069, never a whole Persian phrase
why: Isolating a whole Persian phrase as one LTR run reverses it; isolating only the numeric run fixes bidi without touching the text
numbers: LRI U+2066 / PDI U+2069 around the digits only; e.g. پخ + iso(۴۵) + درجه
do: const iso = s => U+2066 + s + U+2069; then concatenate: text + iso(digits) + text
antipattern: Wrapping پخ ۴۵ درجه — شعاع ۲ میلیمتر in a single isolate and reversing the sentence

rule: Keep the unit inside the same isolate as the number, never in a sibling span
why: The unit left outside the isolate is exactly the character that jumps in the «۴۰/۰ ±mm» bug
numbers: ± is ET/neutral and mm is class L; the number is class EN, so ≥ 3 bidi classes must sit in one isolate
do: Put number, separator and unit in one dir=ltr isolate; for a percent sign inside an RTL flex row put the sign last in DOM inside an LTR island
antipattern: ۴۰/۰ ±mm reading with the unit on the wrong side and ± attached to the wrong end

rule: In canvas, put the isolate characters inside the drawn string AND set ctx.direction = ltr at the same call site
why: A canvas film has no DOM, so PA.ltr() is unusable; the isolate must live in the string passed to fillText
numbers: ctx.direction = ltr at the numeral call; U+2066/U+2069 inside the string
do: Draw: ctx.direction = ltr; ctx.fillText(iso(digits), x, y); ctx.direction = rtl (or reset)
antipattern: A canvas film that satisfies the numeral rule nowhere because the helper returns an HTML span

rule: Name the canvas isolate helper iso() on the numeral's own line so number-lint recognises it
why: number-lint's ISO regex matches a helper named iso( on the numeral line, so any other name makes a correct film fail the lint
numbers: regex \\biso\\s*\\( on the numeral's own line
do: const iso = s => U+2066 + s + U+2069; and call it on the same line as the numeral draw
antipattern: A correct film failing number-lint because the helper was called ltrWrap

rule: Use Persian separators: thousands U+066C, decimal U+066B, percent U+066A
why: A Latin decimal point inside a Persian number is both a typographic error and a bidi hazard because . is class CS, another neutral
numbers: U+066C thousands, U+066B decimal, U+066A percent; 0 Latin . or , inside Persian numbers
do: Check every number string for Latin separators before capture
antipattern: ۱۲,۵۰۰ with a Latin comma inside a Persian measure

rule: Keep a mask container at least 1.5em tall so a Persian reveal never clips dots or descenders
why: At a tight line-height the dots of پ چ ژ above and the descender of ی below are cut by the mask
numbers: mask height >= 1.5em for Naskh (>= 1.9em Nastaliq); inner run translateY 0.3em to 0
do: Size the overflow wrapper from the measured line box, not from a Latin value
antipattern: A masked Persian line whose dots are sliced flat at the top

rule: Never scale a Persian line below 1.0 as a reveal when its mask is tight
why: Scaling down drags the dots and descenders into the mask edge and clips them
numbers: reveal scale band 1.04 to 1.00; never below 1.0
do: Animate the mask position, not a downward scale, when the line box is tight
antipattern: A settle that shrinks a Persian headline until the yeh tail is cut

rule: Use colour-only per-character spans as the one legitimate per-character device
why: Blink keeps joins when only the colour changes (alreq-gap #222), and because spans lay out in logical order a sweep runs right-to-left for free
numbers: colour-only spans; 0 transform, 0 margin, 0 inline-block on the span
do: For a lock sweep, split into per-character spans and change only fillStyle per frame
antipattern: A per-character sweep implemented with transforms, which isolates the letters

rule: Use integer-count tatweel U+0640 at one or two legal joints for kashida expansion, not letter-spacing
why: Kashida is the authentic Persian elongation inserted inside a word at joints where the script allows it, and the width is the point
numbers: 1-2 joints; integer count of U+0640; hide the integer steps under a fast easing or a short motion blur
do: Animate count = round(k * p) at one legal joint plus a small translateX on the surrounding words
antipattern: Adding tatweel at a non-joining boundary so the word reads as a different letter

rule: Prefer ZWJ U+200D over tatweel when you only want joining control without changing the word's width
why: alreq 4.3.4.2 recommends ZWJ when only joining control is needed, because tatweel changes word length
numbers: ZWJ U+200D for joining control; TATWEEL U+0640 only for a deliberate kashida look
do: Choose the character by intent, not by habit
antipattern: Tatweel inserted where the intent was only to control joining

rule: Do not justify Persian paragraphs
why: Browsers do not implement kashida justification, so justify only stretches inter-word spaces and produces rivers
numbers: 0 text-align justify on Persian copy
do: Set ragged lines and balance them by hand in the line array
antipattern: A justified Persian paragraph with rivers of white running through it

rule: Re-measure Persian text after document.fonts.load(); a mount-time measurement uses the fallback font
why: Persian line boxes are taller than Latin and the fallback face has different advances, so measurement at mount is wrong
numbers: await document.fonts.load() before any measureText; 0 hard-coded Latin character-width grids
do: Load fonts, then measure, then build the layout table
antipattern: A layout built from fallback-font widths that shifts when the real face loads

rule: Keep Nastaliq to <= 5 words at >= 100px and never use it for numbers, labels or captions
why: Nastaliq is the preferred Persian display style but its inclined baseline and deep descenders ruin legibility at small sizes and in stacks
numbers: <= 5 words; >= 100px; line-height >= 1.9; 0 numerals; 0 labels
do: Use Nastaliq for one poetic line or a calligraphic title, nothing else
antipattern: A Nastaliq caption or a Nastaliq data label

rule: Reveal Nastaliq along its own baseline, not with a left-to-right horizontal wipe
why: Nastaliq's baseline is inclined, so a horizontal wipe crosses the script's own direction and a per-word straight-line stagger looks mechanically wrong
numbers: mask reveal along the baseline; per-couplet line reveals; a clip window travelling with the ink
do: Choose a diagonal or per-line mask for Nastaliq rather than the standard inset wipe
antipattern: A left-to-right wipe across a Nastaliq couplet

rule: Never set Persian text inside a CSS mask-image SVG data-URI
why: The data-URI is an isolated document with no page web fonts, so it silently falls back to a system font
numbers: 0 text inside mask-image data-URIs
do: Draw the mask from a gradient or an SVG path; keep the text in the main document
antipattern: A masked reveal whose Persian renders in a fallback face

rule: Never use hand-drawn dot-matrix pixel Persian digits
why: Hand-drawn 5x7 Persian digit bitmaps were illegible in this repo: ۲ read as ٣ and ۴ as a blob
numbers: 0 pixel-font Persian digits; rasterise the real font or abandon the treatment
do: If a pixel register is wanted, render the real Persian glyph and posterise it, or drop the numbers
antipattern: A dot-matrix ۲ read as an Arabic ٣

rule: Size a numeral cell from the measured Persian glyph, never from a Latin digit cell
why: A Persian digit at large size can exceed a Latin-sized cell and be sliced by overflow hidden
numbers: cell width >= measureText of the widest Persian digit at the target size
do: Measure ۰-۹ at the real size and set the cell from the widest
antipattern: An odometer slicing the top of a ۴

rule: Declare six palette tokens per film: ink, page, surface, accent, signal, shadow-1..3
why: Zero CSS custom properties is the mechanism by which palettes go ad hoc scene by scene, and every film scanned declared zero
numbers: 6 tokens; declared as CSS custom properties AND mirrored in a JS object for canvas fills
do: Put the token block at the top of the film and read every colour from it
antipattern: Navies then greens then browns then purples with no shared anchor

rule: Keep surface at least 12% L* away from page
why: Closer than that and the object disappears into the field it sits on
numbers: >= 12% L* between surface and page; >= 15% L* between adjacent depth planes
do: Compute surface from page in HSL and widen the gap until the measured L* delta passes
antipattern: A card whose fill is within 3% L* of the page it floats on

rule: Hold the area budget at roughly 60% page, 30% surface, 10% accent plus signal across the film
why: An arbitrary palette gives every scene the same importance so nothing leads and nothing resolves
numbers: 60/30/10 by screen area across the film; accent plus signal <= 10%
do: Measure the budget on a contact sheet of the film, not per scene
antipattern: Five scene colours each given equal area plus a fifth end-card world

rule: Budget the signal colour at a maximum of 2 uses per scene and 1 per frame
why: Signal only works while it is scarce
numbers: <= 2 signal uses per scene; <= 1 per frame; signal is a different hue from accent
do: Count the signal instances per scene in the scene table before building
antipattern: Signal orange used on five objects in one frame so it stops signalling

rule: Let the page token be a hue, never a neutral grey
why: The page is the film's colour identity; a grey field carries no world
numbers: page saturation >= 12%; the page hue becomes the shadow family too
do: Pick the page from the palette row, then derive shadows from it
antipattern: A grey field with objects on it and no world identity

rule: Give accent one job: the brand mark and the primary CTA only
why: Two accents means the audience does not know what the frame is asking them to look at
numbers: 1 accent per film; accent area <= 10% of the film
do: Keep the accent out of scenery; reserve it for the logo and the button
antipattern: The accent used as a general decorative colour on shapes

rule: Scene tinting is a value or saturation shift of the page; introducing a new hue family is a defect
why: Tinting keeps one world; recolouring creates a slideshow of worlds
numbers: per-scene shift of page within +/-12% L* or +/-10% saturation; 0 new hue families after scene 1
do: Derive each scene's page from the film page by an HSL delta
antipattern: Navy to green to brown to purple as scene colours with no narrative logic

rule: Name exactly one hero-contrast frame per film in the header
why: If two frames claim the peak, neither lands and the film has no climax
numbers: 1 named frame where contrast, scale and colour all peak; ideally the end card
do: Write the hero-contrast frame id into the header and build the film toward it
antipattern: Every scene at maximum saturation so no scene peaks

rule: Keep the end card in the film's own page hue family
why: A bright end-card world reads as another film; the finale must share palette, background family and typography
numbers: same page hue family; same white token; 0 new hue families in the end card
do: Choose the end card palette from the film tokens, not from a fresh idea
antipattern: A blue radial sunburst end card as the film's fifth colour world

rule: State the accent budget for each scene in the scene table
why: An unstated budget drifts; a stated one can be checked on the still
numbers: accent plus signal area per scene stated as a percentage; target <= 10% of frame area
do: Add an accent-budget column to the scene table and measure it on the still
antipattern: An accent that quietly grew to cover a third of the frame

rule: Grade warm-to-cool across the film so the ending is not a different world
why: A single global temperature split across the film gives continuity and a destination without adding a hue family
numbers: page saturation shift up to 10%; key-hue temperature slide of 6-14% over the run; 0 hue-family change
do: Interpolate the page/surface tint from t across the whole timeline, one delta per token
antipattern: Warm open and a cold end card that reads as another film

rule: Use a duotone or gradient map to unify imagery into one designed palette
why: It is the fastest way to make mismatched source imagery look like one film
numbers: 2 hues; grayscale contrast 1.1; one multiply layer for highlights, one screen layer for shadows
do: Grayscale the layer, then multiply a shadow hue and screen a highlight hue
antipattern: Teal-and-orange duotone at full saturation

rule: Use at least two different named easings per film and name the job each easing serves
why: A film whose every beat uses the same easing has no motion language
numbers: 2+ distinct named easings; jobs: enter outCubic 0.35-0.55s, reveal outExpo 0.5-0.9s, settle outBack 0.3-0.45s, impact spring 0.6-1.2s with d 0.35-0.6, ambient inOutSine 2-6s
do: Write the easing next to each animation in the scene table; the runtime already ships outCubic, inCubic, inOutSine, outBack, outExpo and a damped spring
antipattern: ease. called 3 times in a 261-line film, i.e. linear motion throughout

rule: Ban linear for any object's own entrance
why: Linear entrance reads as a slide, not as motion with intent
numbers: 0 linear entrances; linear is allowed only for a constant-rate scrub such as a route draw
do: Route the entrance through outCubic or outExpo
antipattern: A headline that slides in at constant speed

rule: Add anticipation before every fast move: 3-8px against the direction for 80-150ms
why: Anticipation is what makes a moving object read as intending the move
numbers: 3-8px travel against the direction; 80-150ms before the move; in canvas, an anti offset added to the lerp
do: Add anti = -dir * 6 * (t < 0.09 ? 1 : 0) style offset during the first 90ms
antipattern: A prop that starts moving with nothing leading the move

rule: Mandatory secondary action on anything that moves: follow-through, overlap and a settle after the stop
why: A rigid object that starts and stops with nothing following it reads as unfinished
numbers: follow-through lag 60-120ms; settle present on every arriving prop; use pa-chain for a lagging chain
do: Chain the trailing element 2-4 frames behind the leader, or use PA.chain(headAt, n, delay, rest)
antipattern: A rigid billet in every frame with no settle, roll or dust follow-through

rule: Stagger grouped elements at 60-90ms offsets, never simultaneously
why: A simultaneous entrance of a group reads as one object, not as a list
numbers: 60-90ms per item; for text, per line 55ms or per word 50ms; per word stagger 40-70ms for Persian
do: p_i = ease(prog(T, t0 + i*0.06, dur))
antipattern: Every item in a list appearing on the same frame

rule: Settle heavy props with the closed-form spring, not with integration
why: The runtime already ships a closed-form damped spring, so overshoot and settle cost nothing and stay seek-safe
numbers: ease.spring(t,k,d); k ~ 95, d ~ 0.42 gives ~89% arrived at 0.2s; v clamped to [0,1.25]
do: const v = clamp(ease.spring(p, 95, 0.42), 0, 1.25); pos = lerp(from, to, v) + anti
antipattern: A drop implemented by integrating velocity per frame, which breaks out-of-order seek

rule: Never animate a spring arrival by scaling the prop from zero, and never let the settle make the prop invisible
why: A settle implemented as height * spring(t) hides a heavy prop for the first ~0.2s and puts it off-frame if the travel shares the parameter
numbers: size/orientation band around 1: sy = 1 - 0.10 * (1 - v); never scale from 0; roll a few degrees; anti offset 6-10px
do: Draw the prop at its true size times a band around 1, and move it with lerp plus anti
antipattern: An empty stage at the top of the scene because the prop scaled from zero

rule: Start a scene's first copy block at the cut plus 0-2 frames and finish it within 12 frames
why: If the copy enters over 14-16 frames the first reviewable frame 0.3s after the cut is a half-transparent headline on an empty stage
numbers: first block at cut + 0-2 frames, complete within 12 frames; later blocks may lag
do: Set t0 for the first text block to the cut time, not to the scene's middle
antipattern: A half-faded headline on an empty stage at the first reviewable frame

rule: Never move or ease the HUD layer
why: A HUD that migrates across the frame is a defect, not a style
numbers: 0 motion on HUD elements between scenes; the counter and the label hold one anchor for the whole film
do: Draw the HUD from a single anchor computed per ratio, once
antipattern: A counter moving from frame centre to the left edge and ثانیه stranded 700px from its numeral

rule: Make heavy props land after the light and the atmosphere do
why: Weight is communicated by who arrives last
numbers: heavy prop arrives after the light pool and the motes have settled; light props lead with outExpo
do: Order the layers' arrival times in the scene table so the prop is last
antipattern: Everything in the scene landing on the same frame

rule: Keep deliberate holds: some beats have nothing moving
why: A film with no holds has no rhythm and no place for the eye to rest
numbers: 1-2 holds of 0.4-1.0s per 15-20s film; ambient drift continues during a hold
do: Mark the hold in the scene table and only let the ambient layer move
antipattern: Every frame carrying a new moving object

rule: Lock rhythmic light and beam angles to a beat-derived zero crossing, never a free rotation
why: Free rotation drifts against the music within a few seconds
numbers: angle = offset * sin(pi * (beat - hit0) / period); 0 free rotation on rhythmic elements
do: Drive the beam angle from the beat clock so it crosses the subject exactly on the grid
antipattern: A rotating light that is a few frames off the beat by the end of the shot

rule: Keep camera keys in scene-local time and reset the transform before the type layer
why: A scene-local clock stops the macro push-in from starting at the film's zero; resetting keeps text from being scaled
numbers: 1 PA.camera per scene built from local seconds since that scene's cut; setTransform(1,0,0,1,0,0) before the type pass
do: Build the camera from local keys, draw the world, reset, then draw the type layer
antipattern: A macro push-in that starts at the film's t=0 and a headline scaled by the camera

rule: Use a differentiated camera vocabulary: macro push-in 1.00 to 1.14 over 2s outCubic, pull-back 1.06 to 0.90 inOutSine, and a 14px vertical offset over 26 frames on every cut
why: Three named moves are enough to give a film a camera language without repeating one shot
numbers: macro push 1.00 -> 1.14 over ~2s outCubic; pull-back 1.06 -> 0.90 inOutSine; 14px vertical over 26 frames per cut
do: Build one PA.camera per scene from those key sets scaled to the shot's framing
antipattern: One identical camera treatment for every scene

rule: Prefer camera moves over cuts where the world is continuous
why: A continuous world with a camera move keeps the actor centred and does not manufacture a new world
numbers: use lib/pa-camera.js keys, follow and pathFollow; cuts only where a new world is intended
do: Reach for the camera track first; cut only when the world changes
antipattern: Cutting between seven frames of the same stage

rule: Keep camera shake at or under 0.4 degrees and 0.3 percent scale, driven by noise(t)
why: Above those amplitudes a shake reads as a broken render rather than as handheld weight
numbers: <= 0.4 degrees rotation; <= 0.3% scale; source is noise(t), never Math.random
do: Add shake = 0.4 * noise(t * speed) to the camera rotation only
antipattern: A shake strong enough to make the frame look unstable

rule: Pair a whip pan with a directional blur, and only as a cut-hider
why: Whip pan without motion blur reads as a jump cut; with it, the blur is the transition
numbers: 1-3 frames of travel; directional blur proportional to camera speed; hide one cut only
do: Compute the blur from the camera's own speed at t, so it is still a pure function of t
antipattern: A fast camera pan with sharp edges, which looks like a glitch

rule: Zoom in log space so a push-in reads as an optical zoom rather than an accelerating slide
why: Linear zoom accelerates perceptually; log-space zoom is constant and reads as a lens
numbers: zoom keys expressed as log(scale); pathFollow and log zoom already available in pa-camera.js
do: Use the camera's log zoom helper instead of lerping a scale value
antipattern: A push-in that starts slow and ends violently

rule: Reframe the camera per ratio rather than re-cropping one framing
why: The 16:9 hero is limited by frame height, so its width grows and its placement moves
numbers: 9:16 horizon and floor line 640/1230; 16:9 400/700; hero moves stage-left in 16:9
do: Give each ratio its own camera anchor and hero placement in the layout table
antipattern: The 16:9 stage being the 9:16 stage with more field

rule: Use a 12-column grid in 9:16 and a 16-column grid in 16:9 with 24px gutters
why: A stated grid is what makes every scene look like it came from one film
numbers: 12 columns 9:16; 16 columns 16:9; 24px gutter; margins from the envelope rule
do: Put the grid in the per-ratio layout table and place every element on a column edge
antipattern: Free-placed elements that never line up between scenes

rule: Hold the hero at or above 25 percent of frame height in 9:16 and 22 percent in 16:9 at the hero moment
why: Scale is how a film declares what it is about; the existing hero >= 12% figure is a watermark, not a hero
numbers: hero >= 25% of frame height in 9:16; >= 22% in 16:9; measured on the text or the subject, never on the largest decorative element
do: Measure the hero's height fraction on the still at its hero moment
antipattern: A prop at roughly 8% of frame area in the middle of a vast dark wall

rule: Change framing, background family, entrance direction or hero scale band between every pair of consecutive scenes
why: The audience learns a repeated template by scene two and then predicts every subsequent frame
numbers: 4 variety axes; 0 shared values on any axis between consecutive scenes; >= 3 framing families per film
do: Diff consecutive rows of the scene table on all four axes before building
antipattern: s10: seven frames of one identical stage with a different small object in the middle

rule: Give the hero a floor and the frame a foreground in every scene
why: A small subject floating in emptiness reads as we had one asset; a large dead field reads as we ran out of things to draw
numbers: hero >= 25% height; 1 foreground occluder; 1 named negative-space form
do: Fill the frame from the layout table outward; put the foreground in first
antipattern: A hero at 20% of frame height with the bottom 40-45% an empty striped floor

rule: Fix one HUD/label anchor per film and hold it for every scene and both ratios
why: A migrating HUD is a defect; one anchor is also the cheapest way to make frames feel like one film
numbers: 1 anchor per ratio; the anchor differs between ratios by the envelope, never by scene
do: Compute the anchor once per ratio from the layout table
antipattern: A counter that moves from frame centre to the left edge across the film

rule: Name one dominant idea per frame and let everything else serve it
why: A frame with no dominant idea has no reading order
numbers: 1 dominant idea per frame, stated in the scene table; supporting elements <= 2
do: Write the frame's one idea in the scene table before the build
antipattern: A frame carrying a headline, a list, a chart, a prop and a logo with equal weight

rule: Design the end card as its own artefact with its own grid, hierarchy and safe area, built after the rest of the film
why: The end card is the frame the client screenshots and the audience remembers, and in this batch it got the least per-pixel attention
numbers: own grid, own y ladder, own safe area; 0 text on text; screenshot-clean at 100%
do: Build the end card last, from its own layout table entry, still inside the film's page hue family
antipattern: An end card with a headline over the certificate's own text, a ribbon and seal over the border, and two flat pills

rule: Model the end card on the batch's best frame: a real lockup with logo, headline, subtitle, CTA, legal row and product
why: That frame is the only one in the batch that shows a deliberate visual system, and it is the template to beat
numbers: lockup = stroked hexagon mark + headline + subtitle + one signal CTA + legal row + product; 3-step hierarchy in that order
do: Lay the lockup on its own grid with one signal colour against a near-black field
antipattern: An end card that is two-thirds empty with a stray decorative ring

rule: Keep a decorative band, stripe or ribbon out of any legal or ISO row
why: A hazard band running through an ISO row destroys the one piece of copy the client must be able to read
numbers: 0 overlaps between decorative bands and legal rows; enforce with a region check
do: Compute legal-row boxes first and forbid decoration intersecting them
antipattern: The hazard-stripe band running through the ISO certification row

rule: Compose both ratios from one per-ratio layout table, never as a crop
why: A re-crop is instantly readable as an afterthought, and the per-ratio claim was already made at SKILL.md:28 while three of five films shipped crops
numbers: 1 film.html; 1 layout table with both 9x16 and 16x9 entries; pa-layout.js throws if a ratio is missing
do: Call layout(table, ratio) for every position, size and type value
antipattern: A landscape cut with the hero smaller and the dead floor proportionally larger

rule: Review the landscape cut as its own film, not as a crop of the tall one
why: Defects that are invisible in 9:16 (a cut-off hero, an empty two-thirds) only appear when the landscape is looked at alone
numbers: >= 9 landscape stills looked at, plus transition frames; the landscape end card reviewed at 100%
do: Run a separate review pass on the 16:9 stills with the tall version out of sight
antipattern: A courier pictogram pushed half off the bottom edge of the landscape frame

rule: Preserve the RTL right-hand anchor in both ratios
why: Flipping the anchor edge changes where the eye starts and breaks the reading rhythm
numbers: right anchor in both ratios; the anchor x differs only by the envelope (W-72 vs W-96)
do: Compute the text rail from the right edge in both ratio branches
antipattern: A text stack anchored to the far left of 16:9 leaving the right two-thirds empty

rule: Change at least five things in a genuine re-composition: horizon line, copy rail anchor, type sizes, hero scale band, end-card grid
why: A per-ratio re-composition is a list of decisions, and changing only the field width is a crop
numbers: 5 minimum changes: horizon/floor line 640/1230 vs 400/700; copy rail W-72 vs W-96; headline 66 vs 72, display 92 vs 88, numeral 112 vs 124; hero placement centre vs stage-left; end card one column vs two
do: Write the five diffs into the layout table and check them off
antipattern: Changing only the field width between ratios

rule: Run a grain overlay at 3-8 percent opacity with overlay or soft-light blending
why: Grain kills gradient banding and adds analogue texture; it is the cheapest expensive-looking trick there is
numbers: 3-8% opacity; 20% and above reads as screen dirt; tile 1-3ms
do: One absolutely positioned grain layer at 5% on soft-light over the whole frame
antipattern: A clean gradient with visible banding and no texture

rule: Pre-render 6-10 grain tiles once and swap the tile by frame index; never animate feTurbulence
why: Animating the filter itself is expensive and non-deterministic; the tile swap is 1-3ms and exactly reproducible
numbers: 6-10 tiles, each a data-URI SVG with its own fixed seed, baseFrequency ~0.8, numOctaves 1-2; select tile index = frame % 6
do: Build the tiles at startup; per frame set backgroundImage to tiles[frame % 6] and jitter transform by 1px
antipattern: A live animated feTurbulence that costs tens of ms and cannot be reproduced from t

rule: Build a mesh-gradient background from 3-6 soft radial blobs on a dark field
why: It is the modern premium gradient and it is GPU-composited, so it costs close to nothing
numbers: 3-6 layers; each radial gradient 50-70% extent at a moving centre; restraint is two hues plus one accent
do: Stack radial-gradients in one element and move each layer's centre from noise(index*7.3 + 0.15*p)
antipattern: A saturated rainbow mesh used as a background

rule: Apply an ACES-filmic tonemap to the composited frame
why: Highlights roll off instead of clipping and the whole image gains a film response; it is the difference between CSS colours and a graded image
numbers: Narkowicz 11-instruction fit; ~2-4ms as one fullscreen pass at 1080x1920; exposure 0.9-1.1
do: One full-screen pass at the very end, over the composited frame including the type layer
antipattern: Raw clipping highlights with flat CSS colours and no response curve

rule: Grade in three fixed steps: cool the shadows, warm the highlights at the key, then vignette the corners
why: One grade recipe applied to world and type together is what makes the type belong to the world
numbers: 1 multiply rgba(fill,.20); 2 screen with a radial key gradient 0.13 to 0 centred on the key position; 3 source-over radial shadow-2 vignette 0 to 0.62
do: Draw the world, draw the type, then run the three grade layers over both
antipattern: Grading the world only, so the headline sits on top of a look it does not share

rule: Keep bloom cheap: a quarter-resolution bright pass with two mips, added back
why: A full-resolution bloom with five mips is about ten fullscreen blurs and is structurally too heavy for an 82ms frame
numbers: quarter-res bright pass; 2 mips; add back; not 5 mips and kernel size array [6,10,14,18,22]
do: Downsample, threshold at ~0.7, blur twice at quarter res, add
antipattern: A full-res UnrealBloomPass-class bloom on a 1080x1920 frame

rule: Cap chromatic aberration at 0.5-2px and use it as a lens effect, not as a glitch
why: At small amplitude it reads as a lens; larger it reads as a broken render
numbers: radial offset k such that the R/B displacement is 0.5-2px at the frame edge; sample at uv + (uv-0.5)*k
do: One shader pass sampling R and B at slightly different radii
antipattern: Chromatic aberration at 8px used as a style

rule: Cap a bokeh field at about 30 sprites with one blur and depth-ranked sizes
why: Above that the sprite draw dominates the frame budget and the field stops reading as defocus
numbers: <= 30 sprites; alpha 0.06-0.18; size proportional to depth; one ctx.filter blur for the whole layer
do: Sort sprites by a noise depth key, blur the layer once, draw
antipattern: Hundreds of individually blurred bokeh sprites

rule: Build paper texture from a fixed-seed feTurbulence fractalNoise tile plus one wide gradient
why: A fixed seed makes the texture reproducible from t while still reading as paper
numbers: 1 tile, seed fixed, fractalNoise, 1-2 octaves; plus one linear gradient of 6-12% L* across the sheet
do: Generate the tile once, draw it at 3-6% alpha, overlay the sheet gradient
antipattern: Per-frame random noise, which cannot be reproduced on out-of-order seek

rule: Use a soft luma or gradient matte for every mask edge; never a 1px step
why: A hard 1px edge reads as cheap; a 2-6px feather reads as premium, and it costs nothing
numbers: feather 2-6px or 4-10% of the mask travel; mask-image linear-gradient with a 4-10% transparent band
do: Animate the maskImage gradient stops rather than a clip-path rectangle
antipattern: A one-pixel clip edge that aliases as it moves

rule: Make window.film.seek(t) a pure function of t: frame round(t*30) is fully determined by t
why: Seek in any order must give identical output, so nothing may accumulate between frames
numbers: frame index = round(t*30); 0 state carried across calls; identical hash for the same t on any order
do: Recompute everything from t each call; use PA.rng(seed) or noise(t) for variation
antipattern: rAF physics, Date.now(), scroll position or unseeded Math.random anywhere in the film

rule: Ban CSS animation, transition and scroll-driven effects in a film
why: The compositor owns those clocks, so the frame shown does not correspond to t
numbers: 0 CSS @keyframes and 0 transitions on the capture path; reveals are written as inline styles per frame
do: Drive every reveal from JS in seek(t)
antipattern: A reveal written as a CSS keyframe that renders differently depending on when the screenshot lands

rule: Load assets locally, never from a CDN
why: The film must render offline in headless Chrome with no network
numbers: 0 http(s) URLs in the film source; fonts from work/persian/assets/fonts
do: Copy any asset into the repo and reference it relatively
antipattern: A font or HDRI fetched from a remote host at render time

rule: Begin every scene painter with a full-canvas base fill
why: seek(t) must be a pure function of t including for pixels the scene does not draw; a partial fill leaves the previous frame visible, and captures may seek out of order
numbers: 1 full-canvas fillRect of a palette token at the top of every scene painter and the end card
do: ctx.fillStyle = page; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H) as the first statement of each painter
antipattern: A still showing the end card rendered behind the pallet scene because the frames were sought out of order

rule: Ban frame-integrated effects: temporal accumulation, feedback buffers, per-frame particle physics and GPGPU ping-pong
why: Each of them carries state, so seeking to frame 40 without rendering 0 to 39 gives a different image
numbers: 0 feedback buffers; a bounded 2-3 ghost motion blur computed by literally rendering t-1 and t-2 is allowed because it is stateless
do: Evaluate a closed-form position field at t instead of advecting particles from the previous frame
antipattern: An AfterimagePass-style accumulation with damp 0.96, which is a seek-dependent image

rule: Pre-bake any integration into a table ahead of time instead of integrating inside seek
why: PA.chain.integrate bakes into a table so seek stays a lookup, which keeps determinism and the frame budget
numbers: integrate(f, dt=1/30, tmax=60) runs ahead of time; seek only interpolates the table
do: Bake at load, look up per frame
antipattern: Per-frame integration inside seek(t)

rule: Budget every frame inside 82-350ms at 1080x1920
why: That is the measured capture window; a shot that cannot hit it cannot ship
numbers: 82-350ms per frame at 1080x1920; 540x960 numbers multiply by about 4
do: Read the measured cost from frame-budget.csv before promising a technique
antipattern: A sustained shader effect at about 4fps used across a whole shot

rule: Treat a WebGL transition as an accent: it straddles one cut and lasts at most 14 frames
why: A transition uploads two full-resolution canvases per frame, so on this machine the cost is judged on the seek number, not the screenshot
numbers: <= 14 frames per transition; ~1ms/frame of extra seek time on top of ~3ms/frame for a plain scene; 12-frame window measured on the s10 v3 build
do: Use one transition per cut and render both layers from the same pure scene painter
antipattern: A shader transition running for a second or longer

rule: Map the five mandatory premium techniques to named scenes in the film header before building
why: Rules that are not mapped to a scene do not get built; the audit found the lessons existed in prose and shipped anyway
numbers: 5 techniques: stated key light with a visible consequence, contact shadow plus one real material, three-plane composition, a named easing used for mass, one hero-contrast frame
do: Write the five scene ids into the header; a blank field is a build error
antipattern: A header with empty premium-technique fields and a film with none of them

rule: Treat a blank header field as a build error
why: The standard is used by copying its palette, light, type and premium-technique sections into the film header and filling every field
numbers: 0 blank fields in the header block before the build starts
do: Fill palette tokens, light block, type roles per ratio, hero-contrast frame, premium techniques, variety check, envelope, HUD anchor
antipattern: A film built with no header block and therefore no stated design

rule: Turn prose lessons into mechanical checks, because a lesson that is only prose ships anyway
why: LESSONS-LEDGER L-001 and L-002 describe the exact defects the audit found three days later while SKILL.md already carried a scrim rule and a duplicate-template gate
numbers: 7 existing gates plus 12 proposed visual gates: region overlap, edge distance, L* deltas, per-object fill variance, easing-call coverage, contact shadow presence, value separation, one-white, hero floor, empty-field share, landscape review, end-card check
do: Convert each visual rule into a gate with a numeric threshold that run-gates can measure, and re-gate the frozen file after the last render
antipattern: Recording a craft lesson in prose and shipping the same defect next batch

rule: Never present an estimate as a measurement when quoting frame cost
why: The project's own measured numbers exist only for the 38 shaders in catalog.json at 540x960; halftone, god rays, bloom, LUT, SVG filters and mesh-gradient repaint costs are estimates
numbers: measured: fps at 540x960 in docs/motion/fx/catalog.json; estimated: everything else; 1080p is 4x the pixels of 540x960
do: Label every number measured or estimated in the plan and in frame-budget.csv
antipattern: An estimated cost quoted to the owner as a measurement

rule: Prove a new technique with a measurement before committing a shot to it
why: SwiftShader is CPU WebGL, so an unmeasured technique can cost more than the whole frame budget
numbers: 1 measurement per new technique, at 540x960 minimum, before it enters a shot
do: Render the shader alone at 60 frames and read the fps before writing it into the film
antipattern: Adopting three.js-class work on the assumption that it will be fast enough

rule: Keep at most three type roles and one live text block per region when a canvas film draws text
why: Canvas has no DOM to help, so every overlap is silent and ships; the batch's worst frame is exactly this in DOM
numbers: <= 3 roles per frame; 1 block per region; region boxes disjoint by construction
do: Compute region rectangles per ratio and assert before drawing the second block
antipattern: A canvas headline drawn over a card's own text because the boxes were never compared

rule: Keep the film's mean luminance out of the 0.30-0.70 mid band: land in the dark mode near 0.112 or in the light mode near 0.913
why: The measured library is bimodal, not continuous: the two modes are 8x apart and only 4.4% of 251 posters sit between them, so a muddy mid-tone field is the one value the house never uses
numbers: mean Rec.709 luminance per frame < 0.30 or > 0.70; dark mode mean 0.112; light mode mean 0.913; mid band 0.30-0.70 in <= 4.4% of frames; library is light-dominant at 59.0% light vs 36.7% dark; the typography tree is the dark tree: median 0.1205, 87.2% dark; overall median luminance 0.887, p10 0.0767, p90 0.9485
do: Grade to one mode, measure the frame mean on the still, and set a type-led film on the dark mode (0.112) and an image-led film on the light mode (0.913)
antipattern: A muddy mid-grey field at 0.4-0.6 mean luminance, the band the 251-poster library occupies in only 4.4% of frames

rule: Start a Persian type-led frame on the measured house plate #0D1D2C, not on an invented navy
why: One plate carries the whole typography tree, so an off-plate navy reads as a different library; the pack's 22 pre-merge rows had zero navy page fields
numbers: #0D1D2C is the dominant plate of 89.7% of the 39 typography posters (35/39) and of 4.2% of the 212 shotcraft posters; measured cluster centre #0F1C28 on 44 posters; plate covers median 90.2% of a typography frame vs 77.2% library-wide (p25 57.6%, p75 91.3%)
do: Set the page field to #0D1D2C and keep the plate share near 90% for a type-led frame and near 77% otherwise
antipattern: A tinted navy or a blue-grey field that is close to #0D1D2C without being it

rule: Hold background-vs-ink contrast at the measured typography bar of 5.76:1, and read the 3.98:1 corpus median as an observed floor rather than a target
why: A third of the real library misses AA 4.5:1 because ink is washed by bloom, grain or a coloured photograph; the median is what happens, not what to aim at
do: Measure the WCAG ratio between the dominant background and the dominant ink on the still, then raise the ink until a type-led frame clears 5.76:1
antipattern: Bloom-washed cream type that measures 3.5:1 and is signed off because most of the library does the same

rule: Reach for desaturated gold #B27338 first when a frame needs one accent, then #CE924A, then violet #5B2E6F
why: The measured accent is the pack's saffron family about 20% less saturated; a hotter accent is the tell of an invented palette, and the pack never named an accent hue
numbers: accent hue ranking: #B27338 (7 posters), #CE924A (5), #5B2E6F (5), #36446B (4), #4464B4 (3), #624992 (3); accent area median 1.22% of frame, p90 11.35%, max 32.96%; only 6 of 44 accent posters exceed 10%; 44 of 251 posters (17.5%) carry a saturated accent at all
do: Pick the accent from the measured ranking and keep its area near 1.22% of the frame with 10% as the hard ceiling from BTY-COLOR-010
antipattern: Full-saturation saffron #C6781A or a neon accent used as the house gold

rule: Texture a large plate with a periodic grid of about 56 px pitch instead of leaving it blank
why: BTY-DEPTH-009 holds in the real library only because a 60%-plus plate is gridded; the periodic grid is what stops a 90% field reading as empty, and no texture rule in the pack names a periodic grid or a pitch
numbers: regular grid/dot texture on 94.9% of typography posters (37/39), 79.7% of shotcraft, 82.1% of 251; grid pitch median 56 px at 1920, p25 40 px, p75 72 px, quantisation +-8 px; texture periodicity score median 0.559, p10 0.166, p90 0.753
do: Lay one periodic grid or dot field across the plate and keep the pitch near 56 px at 1920
antipattern: A flat single-colour plate covering more than 60% of the frame with no periodicity anywhere

rule: Frame a type-led poster with an inset frame or long straight rules
why: It is the second house device on the typography tree and the thing that gives a near-empty plate an edge; the pack mentions a border only for the end card
